## Problem and bounded outcome

`openSparseEngineWebSession` accepts `onProgress`, but only the common `loading` and `prefilling` events reach callers. `prepareSparseSources` does not forward the callback, `SparsePcmSessionOptions` has no callback, and sparse response, chunk decode, canonical installation, and warm verification do not report their actual work. App `StemLoadTracker` at `src/lib/mixer/stem-store/gate-machine.ts` already consumes the adapter's stages and declares no-events after 12 seconds or no-bytes after 45 seconds. Successful unseen work therefore looks stalled.

`FlacWorkerPool.run` creates and terminates a worker for every job. The internal worker self-closes on success and never resets its active request. `NativeFlacDecoder.load` fetches and compiles the decoder for every job. Sparse acquisition invokes this path for every packed chunk. In addition, `VerifiedSparsePcmStore.openSession` processes unique sources serially; replacing the pool alone cannot enable concurrent sparse source decoding.

Deliver observable cold and warm preparation, reuse healthy worker realms across chunks and sources during one preparation, compile a decoder module once for a native resolver's fixed asset configuration, and run independent native sparse sources concurrently within the existing device and memory policy. Preserve ordered full-response acquisition within each source, verification authority, memory and credit bounds, all physical cleanup guarantees, and the headless framework-neutral API. The engine does not need changes.

## Public compatibility and progress contract

Keep the existing `StemProgress` stage union and byte kinds. Add `onProgress?: (progress: StemProgress) => void` to sparse session store options, and forward the common session callback through `SparseSourcePreparationInput` and `acquireSparseSources`. Add an optional third context argument to the sparse resolver function containing `onProgress`; existing `(expected, signal)` resolvers and invocations remain valid. Export a named resolver/context type if that avoids repeated public signatures. Sparse direct install/open APIs may gain an optional callback in their existing options objects where necessary to exercise the same implementation; do not replace their current arguments or add product-only event types.

Validate and snapshot any new callback/context fields at the same public boundary as the existing options. Accept only functions when supplied; preserve exact-key admission and the single-read getter protections from issue 62. Finish validating the full declaration set before any storage, resolver, asset, or worker work. A callback is observation, not a cache verification authority: new sparse notification boundaries must contain synchronous observer exceptions, never turn already verified/committed content into `stem.corrupt`, and never mask an operation or finalizer error. Wrap the sparse session callback before common `loading`/`prefilling` emission so this behavior is consistent on that entry point. Preserve existing dense callback failure behavior unless a narrowly justified shared change and its regressions are recorded. No unhandled rejected async callback Promise should be introduced by a declared synchronous callback API.

Use these exact meanings:

| Event | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| `loading` | Session preparation has begun; total is declared source count. |
| `queued` | A particular identity is awaiting actual bounded work admission. Worker values describe the corresponding pool, not unrelated OPFS/pump workers. Include identity and first matching sourceId when available. |
| `probing` | Real container header/manifest acquisition or native metadata work; never an invented percentage or readiness event. |
| `fetching` | Cumulative bytes consumed from this source's one full sparse response, including header and manifest, against its exact admitted container length. Keep `byteKind: "flac"` for compatibility and document that sparse delivery counts container bytes. |
| `decoding` | Cumulative packed active PCM decoded across all chunks of this source, against the full source's canonical PCM size; implicit silence has not been decoded. |
| `ingesting` | Cold canonical work successfully hashed and staged: advances through bounded zero-gap hash work and active PCM after successful write, against the full canonical size. |
| `verifying` | Warm canonical bytes actually hashed, including implicit zeros, against full canonical size. No fetch/decode work on a fully valid warm source. |
| `source-ready` | This identity has passed complete canonical shape/byte/digest verification and either committed marker-last or verified an existing committed generation. Never infer this from a progress counter reaching its total. |
| `ready` | Every declared source has an admitted verified descriptor and all acquisition scopes have settled successfully. Emit once, after the all-source barrier and cancellation check. `sourcesReady` and `sourcesTotal` both count declarations, including aliases. |
| `prefilling` | Existing engine preparation event after source preparation. It does not substitute for source progress. |

Counters are finite, nonnegative safe integers, never exceed their declared totals, and are monotonic for `(operation, identity, stage, byteKind)`. Never aggregate different identities into one event, reset a cumulative counter for each chunk, multiply by alias count, or add decode and ingest as two copies of canonical work. The app intentionally folds decoding/ingesting into one canonical-work span using a maximum; canonical ingest reports actual full-source positions, including zero work, so cold all-silent sources can advance without FLAC workers.

The sparse response cursor owns delivery counting. Do not count the same response bytes again when a finite chunk source feeds the decoder. An optional/missing HTTP Content-Length must remain supported: after bounded header/manifest admission the exact encoded container length is authoritative, subject to existing content-length/EOF checks. Header bytes consumed before that total is known must be included in the first truthful cumulative event. Preserve one bodyless full GET per source and existing locator/request semantics; do not turn progress into additional network requests.

Keep source-level counters independent across concurrent operations, including two opens of the same identity. Intermediate source progress can use the first declaration's sourceId; issue `source-ready` once per declared alias after its shared descriptor is admitted, without repeating verification. Return declaration order unchanged. Earlier successful sources may emit readiness before a later source fails, because their valid commits remain. After terminal failure/cancellation, detach callbacks and do not issue further work or aggregate `ready`. Check cancellation before final readiness and again at the existing public handoff; readiness is a verified-source fact, not a promise that an observer cannot synchronously cancel later handoff.

Emit bounded progress during real body reads, PCM blocks, writes, and zero-hash blocks. Never use a periodic heartbeat to fake activity or relax the app watchdog. Coalesce high-frequency notifications using one operation-local bounded counter/time threshold (target at most roughly 10–20 callbacks/second/source during fast sustained work), while always delivering stage starts, meaningful ongoing progress, and final counter/readiness boundaries. No accumulating event queue, whole-file buffering, timer surviving teardown, or timer-only progress. A slow stream that advances within watchdog thresholds must remain observable; a stream that does no work must still stall/refuse under existing deadlines.

## Reusable worker and decoder architecture

Use the existing private pool and worker protocol. A job still owns its own request ID, input slot, output credits, decoder instance, nonshared fixed 2 MiB linear memory, hash state, diagnostics, and abort/watchdog state. Reuse the worker JavaScript realm and immutable compiled module; do not reuse mutable decoder instances, grow/shared decoder memory, use one worker to simulate parallel decoding, or introduce codecs/fallbacks.

Separate module loading from decoder instantiation. A lazy single-flight loader owned by a native resolver/pool's snapshotted decoder URL performs one fetch and `WebAssembly.compileStreaming`, preserving HTTP status, `application/wasm` MIME, ABI, and fixed-memory validation. Pass the resulting `WebAssembly.Module` to worker jobs via structured clone, not a transfer list; instantiate independently inside each worker. Compiled modules contain shareable code, not shared decoder state. A repeated concurrent first request must join the same compile Promise. Keep at most the fixed configuration's one module/pending compile per resolver; no unbounded module-level URL map or global worker singleton. No decoder asset request on warm or all-silent opens. Asset/compile/clone errors remain typed, bounded, and observable to the operation; there is no silent per-worker recompile fallback. A failed single-flight load must not permanently poison a later independent attempt. One cancelled waiter must not abort a shared load still required by another active waiter. Last-owner cancellation must stop abortable asset work and make eventual non-abortable compile completion inert.

Healthy jobs complete a reset handshake: destroy the instance successfully, clear decoder/hash/input/runnable/credit references and timing counters, reset the active request, then acknowledge completion/idle for that exact request. A completion acknowledgement may serve as reset proof only if it is sent after this reset and the host also finishes its existing input-lane/finite-source verification. No return to the pool based merely on receipt of the last PCM block. In particular, compressed digest/EOF and host chunk PCM checks must still succeed before reusable success. A decode, protocol, destroy, message-clone, timeout, or cancellation failure poisons the worker; terminate it and replace it only after release is physically safe. Late replies/credits for prior IDs cannot affect a later job, and duplicate/out-of-order completion cannot reinsert an already leased worker. Do not leave the old `scope.close()` on the successful path.

Keep two outstanding PCM output credits, one fixed shared input slot, 384 KiB maximum decoder output, 128 KiB sparse span slices, bounded download bodies, and existing write backpressure. A completed job may leave an output block with its consumer: either retain its job reservation until that output is released, or explicitly keep those residual buffers charged before another job begins. Returning a worker early must never permit an unbounded number of queued/completed jobs' PCM blocks. Dispose old request listeners and suspend/clear its watchdog before reuse; a previous job cannot cancel a healthy successor. `onTerminated` currently releases a runnable bit: distinguish actual physical termination from successful job/runnable release rather than retaining misleading semantics.

Pool lifetime is one preparation epoch, not playback lifetime. Acquire an internal retention lease before source preparation and release it only after all source iterators, input lanes, borrowed blocks, physical writers, and worker jobs settle. Final release drains/rejects queued work as appropriate, terminates idle/active workers, and waits for physical finalization before resolving. It is idempotent. Native direct resolver streams retain their own scope until normal EOF, cancellation, or iterator return; existing callers do not need to discover a new public `close()` method. Overlapping preparations sharing one resolver must not close each other's workers. Do not eagerly create the pool width; only construct workers needed by queued jobs. Successful worker construction count during one healthy preparation must be bounded by peak eligible concurrency, rather than chunk or source count. Failed-worker replacement is counted separately.

A small internal WeakMap registration, analogous to current dense `registerFlacResolver`/`flacResolverScheduling`, should associate the exact native sparse resolver function with its computed widths and preparation-retention hook. The store uses this metadata without exposing pool mechanics in the public contract. Plain custom resolvers remain valid and sequential. A wrapper around a native function remains a valid resolver but loses private scheduling optimization unless the package explicitly preserves its registration; document this limitation. Direct use of the native function still gets per-stream chunk reuse.

Physical worker reservations must remain bounded even when idle. Releasing an externally shared `BoundedStemAdmission` token while retaining a worker must not allow other pools to exceed its reservation budget. Holding all idle reservations indefinitely must not deadlock another pool that holds source locks. The narrow safe default is to retain privately owned pool reservations within an epoch; for caller-injected shared admission, retaining workers across jobs is optional and a documented one-job physical lifetime is acceptable until safe cross-pool idle arbitration exists. Do not build such an arbitration service merely for this issue. Test this exception explicitly, and never claim all modes reuse workers. Preserve dense resolver behavior and its existing processing policy; shared protocol changes must pass its regression suite.

## Bounded sparse source scheduling

For the exact registered native resolver, replace the serial unique-source loop with bounded Effect scheduling at the existing computed processing width, capped by unique source count. That width already accounts for CPU hints, memory reservation, maximumWorkers, and admission policy; do not blindly spawn `hardwareConcurrency - 1`, invent a second source-count policy, or widen existing legacy/opt-in memory behavior. The resolver retains its independently bounded download admission. The default on eligible machines must demonstrate more than one active decoder for independent cold sources. One source with multiple chunks remains serial because it owns one ordered HTTP cursor; parallel chunk ranges or whole-chunk buffering are out of scope. Warm-only or custom resolver calls can keep sequential scheduling.

Continue using the existing SparseProgram/ManagedRuntime and Effect scopes; do not add another runtime, unbounded Promise.all, bespoke promise scheduler, or call public Promise store methods from internal Effects. Complete admission/snapshot/deduplication first. Each unique identity gets its own scope and lock; release its source lock before another source occupies that task slot. Preserve source declaration order in the returned lease even when completion order differs. Do not retain multiple source locks in a task or use all-source filesystem transactions.

Retained metadata accounting stays `maximumMetadataBytes` with the accepted per-declaration and per-unique-index charges. Charge each descriptor atomically before inserting it in the retained map; a concurrent lost update cannot overspend the budget. A budget refusal yields no lease and cancels/settles sibling work, while earlier valid commits remain. State the changed transient bound explicitly: concurrency C permits at most C accepted bounded source/index scratch states outside the retained-map budget, replacing the former one-source transient bound. Do not collect all uncharged descriptors before checking the budget. Keep metadata, worker-buffer, and response bounds distinct and record their worst-case multiplication by C in the resource documentation.

On any failure, stop scheduling new sources, interrupt siblings, propagate their cancellation to actual body readers/input slots/writers, await finalizers, and preserve the original failure plus cleanup Causes. Shared resolver preparations and a subsequent session must recover without leaked credits, locks, counters, or dead workers. Do not use an aggregate session timeout; current progress deadlines remain independent of album duration and source count. Detached successful leases, metadata-only presence, marker-last installation, no repair of corrupt committed sparse sources, and session pump/backend teardown order remain unchanged.

3. **Bounded parallel sparse preparation.** Register native scheduling/lifetime metadata and use it in the existing Effect store preparation. Prove metadata charging, lock release, sibling cancellation, shared-resolver independence, and pooled output/physical resource bounds. 4. **Packed/browser qualification and app consumption.** Build and pack the candidate, install it in a fresh consumer, run the browser and package gates below, then test the candidate from the isolated app worktree. ## Distinguishing acceptance tests

Use existing tests/harnesses where possible. A test must fail on the old defect, not merely assert calls to the new helper.

**Progress and integrity**

- Observe the public `openSparseEngineWebSession({onProgress})` seam on cold mixed sparse sources, warm sources, and a completely silent source. Assert identities, callback forwarding into the store/resolver, valid units/totals, in-flight byte changes, and loading → source readiness → aggregate ready → prefilling ordering. Silence causes real canonical progress without constructing a decoder.
- A packed source with at least two unequal chunks, several active intervals, and leading/interior/trailing silence proves cumulative delivery/decode/ingest counters. The second chunk must advance beyond the first chunk endpoint instead of restarting. Independent interleaved sources cannot exchange totals. Aliases verify once and all receive readiness without double counting bytes.
- Warm hashing and cold zero hashing emit multiple advances for large logical gaps while retaining bounded buffers and cancellability. Hashing all logical bytes is still mandatory. A checksum or byte-count failure after the last progress byte must emit neither source-ready for that identity nor aggregate ready.
- No-source sessions, absent Content-Length, corrupt/missing generation, invalid manifest, truncated body, wrong FLAC/PCM digest, abort during callback, callback throw, and terminal cleanup failure preserve the stated readiness and error behavior. Malformed new callback options refuse before I/O; callback observation cannot corrupt a valid cache entry.
- Feed actual adapter-shaped sequences into the app's existing tracker with a controlled clock: cold work lasting more than 12 seconds and more than 45 seconds overall remains loading while real bytes advance; warm/zero work behaves likewise. A truly silent/no-byte stream still reaches the existing watchdog result. Do not change timeouts to make the regression pass.

**Workers, modules, concurrency, and physical ownership**

- Real worker: run multiple distinct valid jobs through the same worker, verify exact canonical bytes/digests, and prove per-job state reset/fresh instance. Follow a cancelled, corrupt, crashed, stalled, destroy-trapping, or clone-failing job with a good job: poisoned workers are terminated, replacements succeed, and late prior-request traffic cannot corrupt them.
- Three or more chunks on one source construct one healthy FLAC worker within its epoch. N independent multi-chunk sources construct no more than C healthy workers, complete more than C jobs, and actually overlap decodes when C > 1. Assert worker physical alive/terminated counts and outstanding buffers, not only scheduling counters.
- Instrument the module loader: one asset fetch and one compile invocation for concurrent first use, then multiple independent instantiations with distinct fixed nonshared memories. Different configured decoder URLs cannot share a wrong module. Failed load followed by a later fresh attempt can retry; one cancelled concurrent waiter does not fail a surviving waiter. Last-owner cancellation produces no late worker/job resurrection.
- A slow/unreleased PCM consumer retains output accounting and backpressure across job boundaries. Abort while queued, during asset load, waiting for input/output credit, between chunks, and during OPFS finalization leaves zero queued jobs, listeners, runnable bits, held borrows and physical workers after epoch close. Epoch close waits for pending physical cleanup and preserves cleanup failure; tests must not satisfy this by checking only logical Promise settlement.
- A one-worker/8 MiB policy creates at most one physical worker even with many sources; eligible CPU/memory policy creates multiple. Two pools sharing caller admission cannot exceed its total reservation and cannot hang because an idle pool monopolizes admission. If the documented conservative shared-admission exception is used, assert its termination behavior explicitly.
- Native bounded store scheduling: all declarations are validated before I/O; at most C source tasks are active; aliases dedupe; out-of-order completion preserves declarations; budget charges are exact under concurrent completions; failure cancels siblings after physical cleanup; earlier commits persist. Two sessions opening the same identities in opposite order do not deadlock. One preparation ending cannot terminate another preparation's still-active jobs.

**Real packed fresh-consumer proof**

Run the package's actual archive through its existing fresh Vite consumer; use installed archive imports and packaged Worker/Wasm URLs, not `src`, producer `dist`, or symlinks into the worktree. Retain archive SHA-256, candidate revision/tree hash, lock/install provenance, browser version, invocation, and result JSON/logs outside tracked paths. If dependencies are copied as in the existing browser harness, say so accurately and additionally retain a normal clean install of the same archive for import/type/build qualification.

Extend `scripts/browser-packed.mjs --indexed-sparse` or a small focused sibling to use several independent non-silent sparse identities, multiple unequal chunks per source, and warm/all-silent paths. The existing assertion that worker count equals chunk count must become a reuse assertion. Count actual Worker construction, job start/completion IDs, termination, decoder-asset HTTP request count, and compile invocations. A `Map<url,mime>` proves only asset identity, not the number of requests; add request counters. Disk/memory HTTP cache hits do not prove a single fetch or compilation. Verify that each worker handles more than one job where the fixture allows it and no healthy worker is self-closed between jobs.

Prove positive real-worker overlap on an eligible configured device profile using shared runnable-worker instrumentation or another direct concurrent-processing observation; two launched workers alone are insufficient. Use large enough real fixture jobs to make overlap measurable. Record elapsed cold preparation and width=1 versus eligible-width measurements as context, without a flaky fixed speedup threshold. Do not skip a failed positive-concurrency assertion by relabeling the browser ineligible after the fact. Preserve actual playable output/seek and warm-cache no-network checks from the current browser harness.

Available local Chromium: `CHROME_EXECUTABLE=/home/bl/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`. Verify its existence when qualifying; the harness's default discovery did not find it at baseline. Network asset and worker failures, console/page errors, and readiness/cleanup counters must be included in the browser evidence.

## Independent review and completion record

A fresh Astra medium reviewer reads this numbered spec, the frozen candidate diff, and relevant production/test code without participating in implementation. It reruns focused adversarial discriminators and checks actual archive/browser evidence. In particular, review stale-request reuse, instance-memory independence, shared admission/idle physical memory, residual output credits, asset load cancellation, response byte double counting, concurrent metadata budget admission, callback exception containment, final readiness versus digest, and all sibling/session teardown races.

The reviewer returns PASS or concrete reproducible findings, separating release blockers from optional improvements. Root may assign bounded fixes to Luna max and then request fresh re-review of changed risks. A successful implementation self-report alone does not complete this issue.

Append the final candidate commit/tree, changed paths, checkpoint/evidence locations, archive digest, browser profile/results, app candidate qualification, independent reviewer verdict, unresolved blockers, and release readiness here and synchronize the issue. Completion means a concrete implemented and independently verified candidate with no remaining required work or newly introduced gate failure. It does not claim an npm release, production dependency update, merge, or deployment.
